next_question: Given that linear combination recipes cannot break OECD/COINr degeneracy (mathematical identity: mean always ranks between originals when canonical<weighted strictly), should the MIXED outcome program pivot to (a) a structurally non-linear third recipe (DOM hierarchy depth, conditional inclusion based on element relationships, semantic role weighting) that could produce rankings outside the canonical-weighted range, (b) an alternative MIXED decision rule entirely (density ratio between canonical and weighted as a continuous sensitivity metric, or ranking reversal rate across definitions), or (c) abandon dominance-based MIXED handling and restrict density metric use to recipe-insensitive task-definition pairs if definition choice is shown to be the primary resolution lever?
why_next: The linear meta-analytic mean recipe is mathematically guaranteed to rank between canonical and weighted, making it a trivial interpolation that cannot break degeneracy. This is a closed mathematical fact, not an empirical finding requiring replication. The MIXED outcome decision rule remains the blocking unresolved question for C-MEAS-VALID. Three materially orthogonal pivot paths exist: (a) non-linear structural recipe that could cross the canonical-weighted ordering boundary, (b) alternative continuous sensitivity metric replacing discrete dominance, (c) recipe-insensitive subset restriction. The intel lane is best positioned to evaluate which pivot maximizes information gain before the runtime lane removes the locatableSample cap for full-DOM re-run.

do_not_assume: Do NOT use OECD/COINr framework with only 2 recipes to justify recipe choice — dominance is necessarily degenerate (0%/100%) by construction, not by scientific finding.

Do NOT assume the 31x (recomputed from 84.7x) cross-recipe density ratio is a validated scientific result — it is observed on truncated-first-20 data (locatable_sample cap 20) and may change with full DOM enumeration.

Do NOT assume the OECD/COINr framework has been validated for SPIDER's density metric — the 2-recipe experiment demonstrated it is NOT informative in the 2-recipe setting (construct failure), and this 3-recipe experiment demonstrated linear combinations cannot fix the degeneracy.
Do NOT assume SPIDER-to-field applicability mappings are established results — they are interpretive analogies bounded by audit findings.
Do NOT assume the non-systematic literature search captured all relevant prior art — a formal systematic review may yield additional methods.

Do NOT assume the FALSIFIED-IN-SETTING conclusion generalizes to full-DOM — truncated-first-20 is a non-representative slice. However, the mathematical tautology (linear mean always between originals) IS general for any setting where canonical<weighted strictly.
Do NOT assume the per-iteration recipe is universally canonical beyond this experiment's scope.
Do NOT assume the density metric is entirely useless — ordering-based discrimination is definition-sensitive and recipe-sensitive, not that density values are uninformative.
Do NOT assume recipe choice is a nuisance parameter — it is a MATERIAL determinant of the scientific conclusion.
Do NOT assume C-MEAS-VALID status changed from this experiment — it remains EXPERIMENTAL; this experiment attempted framework operationalization, not empirical measurement validation.
Do NOT assume quantitative parent values are reliable — deviations exceed frozen thresholds (M1 means ~35% offset between producer and recomputed).
Do NOT assume the MIXED outcome decision rule is resolved — it remains open pending non-linear recipe or alternative framework.
Do NOT assume non-linear third recipes will succeed where linear ones failed — the 31x gap may be too large for ANY recipe to cross the canonical-weighted boundary on some task-definition pairs.
Do NOT assume the density ratio approach (alternative to dominance) is viable — it has not been tested and may have its own degeneracy issues.
